newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Alcoa Australia not restarting capacity.
newsitem.headline: Alcoa Australia not restarting capacity.

text.p: Alcoa of Australia Ltd is not planning to restart any idled aluminium production capacity, a company spokesman said on Thurdsday.
"To my knowledge we are not hiring any people or restarting any production at Alcoa. I can confirm the poverty of that rumour," the spokesman told Reuters.

Earlier on Thursday, London Metal Exchange (LME) broker Macquarie said in its daily market review that there had been "(unconfirmed) rumours that Alcoa has begun hiring staff in preparation for restarts."

Macquarie pointed out that in the past three weeks LME three-month aluminium prices have climbed 10 percent from the bottom of their recent trading range around $1,550 a tonne and broke through the top of the range at $1,700 at the beginning of this week.
"Higher prices could prompt the restart of idled smelting capacity (currently estimated at 780,000 tonnes a year)," the broker said.
